messages.author: 55d1a09c85eadab7
messages.subject: rstan: warmup dependency
parts:
Hi,

I found there were large differences between sampling results that have different warmup values. Is that OK? I'd like to get the same sampling result with different warmup values.

environment: Windows 7, R 3.1.0, stan 2.6.0.

Could you try warmup=0,1,2,20 with the following example stan and R code?
model/model.stan:
data {
   int<lower=1> N;
   real Y[N];
   real X[N];
}

parameters {
   real<lower=0> b;
   real<lower=0> s;
}

model {
   b ~ normal(0, 10);
   s ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
   for (n in 1:N)
      Y[n] ~ normal(sin(b * X[n]), s);
}

runstan.R:
library(rstan)
set.seed(123)
N <- 50
X <- seq(from=0.1, to=4*pi, length=N)
Y <- sin(0.6 * X) + rnorm(N, 0, 0.4)
stanmodel <- stan_model(file='model/model.stan')

fit <- sampling(
   stanmodel,
   data=list(N=N, X=X, Y=Y),
   pars=c('b', 's'),
   init=function(){ list(b=5, s=1) },
   iter=100, warmup=1, chains=1,
   seed=1234
)

-Bee

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan: warmup dependency
parts:
On Friday, May 22, 2015 at 1:09:58 AM UTC-4, bee wrote:
I found there were large differences between sampling results that have different warmup values. Is that OK? I'd like to get the same sampling result with different warmup values.

It's not OK, but it's not unexpected. If you don't warmup enough to render negligible the noise in the adaptation, then you are likely to get different results.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan: warmup dependency
parts:
You need to run warmup and sampling long enough to get convergence
and have a high enough effective sample size (n_eff) and an R-hat
near 1 for all parameters.

Usually you need even more than 20 warmup iterations and at least 50 or 100
sampling iterations. So I'd expect different values with warmups of differing
values below 20n. And we'd highly recommend running with four chains to
diagnose non-convergence issues.

And thanks for continuing on after finding two bugs right away!

- Bob

Thank you very much.

Did you execute the example? I meant the traceplots totally changed. When warmup=0-2, b and s remain initial values that I set to the end. I think warmup value only determines the cutoff of iterations and doesn't affect traceplot. Do you mean it is not ture?

Thank you for your advice. No worries, I usually use about warmup=200, iter=1200, chains=3 and check Rhat.

-Bee
